subject: Silverline hosted commit uplift & rateband reconfiguration

Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning: hosted capacity increase

Hi Neha,

Hope you’re well. As we review Q3 projections, our product team expects a steady 2.8x increase in API traffic for the checkout and recommendations flow beginning July. Current hosted tiers will hit throttles under our existing monthly commit. We want to explore an uplift to an annual committed amount and a corresponding rateband change so we can avoid per-token overage volatility.

Key asks: 
- A simple proposal for a monthly committed uplift (3 options: conservative / expected / aggressive)
- Updated unit rates for each model tier (we primarily use rdl-2.1-mid and embed-lite)
- Any onboarding or migration windows and how soft throttles will be handled during ramp
- Suggested start date and billing implications (prorated for mid-quarter start)

Procurement is looped on this thread (procurement@silverline.com) — they’ll need the pricing sheet and any MSA redlines.

Thanks,
Carla
VP Product
Silverline Systems

Hi Carla — thanks for the details and heads up on the July ramp. I ran a quick sizing with our capacity team and attached a pricing sheet + MAP that covers three uplift profiles (Conservative / Expected / Aggressive) and the recommended ratebands for both generation and embeddings. High level:

- Conservative: +2x monthly commit, standard rateband (no discount)
- Expected: +3x monthly commit, 10% discount on model unit rates
- Aggressive: +4.5x monthly commit, 12% discount + burst cushion for first 90 days

Notes on throttles and ramp: we can enable a soft-burst policy for 30 days to smooth the transition; after that we switch to committed enforcement with automatic billing for overages. If you prefer full commitment with no soft-burst we can price that too (slightly lower unit costs).

Proposed start: 2026-07-01 (prorated invoice for partial month). DocuSign for the amendment is ready — I’ll share the link once we lock terms.

I attached: silverline_pricing_v2.pdf (line-item pricing), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (ops/rollout owner matrix).

If procurement wants vendor terms redlines up front, loop them and we’ll get Legal engaged.

— Neha

Neha / Ben — quick internal:

Read Carla’s ask and your proposal. A few commercial points to confirm before I approve the 10% in the Expected profile:
1) Minimum annual commitment term — do we require 12 months from the prorated start? Any option for 9-month ramps?
2) Burst cushion details — is the aggressive cushion capped (tokens/day) or open? We should limit exposure.
3) Discount stacking — confirm that embedding rates are included in the same band or calculated separately.

Also, is there room for a one-time onboarding credit (covering migration/ops time) to sweeten the deal? If procurement is slow, we can offer a 30-day sign-by window for the Expected discount.

Karthik — I reviewed the numbers with Finance. We can do the following for the Expected profile if they sign the annual amendment within 30 days:

- 10% off generation unit rates and 8% off embedding rates (applied across the committed volume)
- A one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the first month’s invoice to help with migration ops
- Aggressive profile retains a capped burst cushion: up to 20% above daily expected traffic for the first 90 days; overage beyond that billed at committed rates

We should require a 12-month minimum term from the prorated start date to qualify for the discount. Shorter terms get smaller discounts.

I attached a quick cost breakout for the sign-by scenarios. If you want, I can draft the amendment language for Legal to slot into the MSA.
